title: Automakers pivot to humanoids as EV supply chains speed mass production
key_facts: On 8 Aug 2026 Chinese carmaker Xpeng began running an automated production line for humanoid robots in Guangzhou; its IRON robot (178 cm tall) walked off the line on its own at the launch.
Xpeng says more than 80% of the core processes on that line are automated; it did not say which processes.
Xpeng aims to start mass production by the end of 2026 at 1,000 robots a month, first using them in its own stores for guiding visitors, with outside sales from 2027.
Xpeng chief executive He Xiaopeng said more than 85% of IRON's suppliers overlap with its car-parts suppliers (second-quarter earnings briefing last month).
Xpeng's robotics division raised $900 million last month from IDG Capital, Tencent and Alibaba, which the article calls the largest single private round in China's embodied-AI sector.
Hyundai Motor Group plans to deploy Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid at factories from 2028, starting with Hyundai's Metaplant America in the US, and is building capacity for 30,000 units a year.
Tesla is reportedly checking Chinese EV-parts makers as suppliers for its Optimus humanoid ahead of a year-end launch; the article names Zhejiang Sanhua, Ningbo Junsheng and Ningbo Tuopu.

Han Jae-kwon, professor of robotics at Hanyang University, said EV makers already hold much of the humanoid supply chain, and that how many parts a firm makes itself will decide how fast and cheaply it can sell humanoids.
quote_evidence: Xpeng said it has automated more than 80% of the core processes on the Humanoid Robot production line.
Xpeng aims to start mass production by year-end and produce 1,000 Humanoid Robots a month.
Because there is no need to build the entire supply chain from scratch, it can lower parts procurement expense and shorten timelines.
why_it_matters_hint: Carmakers can reuse their car parts supply chains to build humanoid robots, which could make the robots cheaper and sooner.
event_date: Xpeng line opened 8 Aug 2026; article and analysis dated 9 Oct 2026
notes: Analysis feature; the underlying Xpeng launch (8 Aug) and the $900m round (Sept) are before the 8 Oct window, so FOLLOW-UP. Several claims are company statements or 'reportedly' (Tesla suppliers); the 'competitive edge' view is analysts' opinion. Date of the Hyundai 2028 plan not stated.
